questions.q: According to the summary, what separates good debt from bad debt?
a: Good debt funds assets that produce cash
Good debt always comes from family members
Good debt carries the highest available interest
Good debt never has to be repaid
questions.why: Lesson 2 defines good debt as money that helps you build cash-producing assets, while bad debt is borrowed at rates you cannot repay.

questions.q: Which planning tool does the summary recommend for mapping a company's core strengths and weaknesses?
a: A SWOT analysis
A buyer persona
A cash-flow forecast
An equity split
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the masterplan should include a SWOT analysis to define core competencies and weaknesses.

questions.q: Why does the summary say keeping existing customers deserves special attention?
a: Retaining buyers costs less than winning new ones
Loyal buyers never ask for discounts
Existing buyers are easier to advertise to
Retained buyers require no market research
questions.why: Lesson 3 states that acquiring new customers is more expensive than keeping old ones, and loyal buyers also make forecasting easier.

questions.q: What does the summary recommend establishing first in order to attract the right customers?
a: A detailed buyer persona
A larger advertising budget
A second physical location
A cheaper pricing model
questions.why: Lesson 3 says defining your buyer persona is a top priority, since knowing your audience makes targeted strategies possible.

questions.q: What does the summary say about setting ambitious goals for a new business?
a: Aiming high only makes sense with hard work behind it
Goals should stay modest until profits appear
Ambitious goals remove the need for a plan
Goals matter less than the company website
questions.why: Lesson 1 argues that dreaming big is reasonable only when you are determined to put in the work, and goals should match your values.
